LESSON: READING 1.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION: NOTE MAKING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making, part of Strand 1 in Grade 6 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we make notes?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a passage and identify key points to note,

2. work jointly to pick out adverbs used in the passage,

3. read the adverbs aloud with peers,

4. work with peers to use digital devices to search for information on the theme,

5. work jointly to use key points from a story to summarise information,

6. collaborate with peers to peer review written summaries.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a passage and identify key points to note,
2. work jointly to pick out adverbs used in the passage,
3. read the adverbs aloud with peers,
4. work with peers to use digital devices to search for information on the theme,
5. work jointly to use key points from a story to summarise information,
6. collaborate with peers to peer review written summaries.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner contributes to group decision making when using

key points from a story to summarise information.

• Digital Literacy: This is promoted as the learner interacts with technology to search for information on the theme.

4

Values:
● Unity: This is promoted as the learners work harmoniously with peers to review and correct mistakes in the summaries.

● Responsibility: It is nurtured as the learner uses digital devices correctly to search for information on the theme

without diverting to inappropriate sites.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Cultural awareness: This is promoted as the learner interacts with various songs from communities on cultural festivals

and ceremonies.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of note making and summary writing to their reading strategies in English and Kiswahili.
